page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.medium is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by a custom AWS Graviton Arm64 processor. The instance features 1 dedicated physical CPU core running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Furthermore, the instance provides 59 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage directly attached to the virtual machine, along with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It operates without discrete GPUs.

Because benchmark data is not explicitly available for this specific instance tier, performance evaluation relies on its hardware parameters. Operating on an Arm64 architecture with a dedicated core running at 3.3 GHz, it avoids noisy-neighbor resource contention typically associated with shared-core micro-instances. The bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD volume offers low-latency local block storage for workloads requiring direct disk access. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton ARM architecture and high resource density of a small compute instance lower operating overhead compared to traditional x86-based equivalents, though memory constraints limit heavy multi-threaded processes.

Key tradeoffs include the relatively limited 2.0 GB memory capacity and single virtual core, which constrain memory-intensive operations or highly parallel applications. Additionally, local NVMe storage is ephemeral and instance-store based, requiring external persistent storage strategies for long-term data retention. The c9gd.medium is well-suited for lightweight compute tasks, small scale microservices, edge web serving, cache nodes, and preliminary testing environments requiring direct NVMe disk access on Arm-based infrastructure.
